question: In an equilateral triangle with side length 'a', what is the ratio of the circumradius to the inradius?
solution: [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__ In an equilateral triangle, the circumcenter, incenter, and centroid all coincide at the exact same point. The centroid divides the median (which is also the altitude) in the ratio 2:1. The longer segment from the vertex to the centroid is the circumradius (R). The shorter segment from the centroid to the base is the inradius (r). Thus, the ratio of circumradius to inradius (R:r) is directly 2:1 without any calculation. **∴ The correct answer is 2:1.**
